newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends near highs on spec, trade buying.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends near highs on spec, trade buying.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures closed a see-saw session stronger on speculative and trade buying near the close, inspired by December's ability to hold above 74.00 cents, market sources said.
Short-covering in October gave the spot-contract a slight boost, but open interest stood at only 3,839 lots, down 513 lots. Tuesday is the first notice day for the October contract.

"We're just playing a waiting game," said Sharon Johnson, an analyst with Frank Schneider and Co Inc. "Folks are still concerned about supply, but they are equally concerned about demand. It's a question of which will eventually win out."
The U.S. Department of Agriculture will release its weekly export report at 0830 EDT Thursday, but expectations are for continued weak demand.
December finished 0.40 higher at 74.45 cents a lb, having ranged from 74.60 to 73.70. Spot-October ended up 0.57 at 73.45, while the back months finished 0.37 higher to 0.15 lower.
Volume was estimated at only 7,000 lots.
